newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb kills seven in India's Punjab state.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills seven in India's Punjab state.

text.p: At least seven people were killed in a powerful bomb blast in India's troubled state of Punjab on Friday, the first major attack in the region since a pro-Sikh party took power in February, police said.
They said the blast near a busy train station in the city of Jalandhar, a business hub in the northern state bordering Pakistan, also injured 10 people.

The blast came as a rude surprise to the agriculture-rich state where years of separatist violence had appeared to be waning recently , crowned by a peaceful election to the local legislature in February.

"After the assassination of Chief Minister Beant Singh, this is the first incident which we suspect to be of militant violence," Mohinder Pal Aulakh, head of the state's police intelligence told Reuters.
Singh was assassinated by a suspected Sikh suicide bomber on August 31 1995.
"We are trying to ascertain the type of bomb used," Gurvinder Singh Aujala, police chief of the Jalandhar region, told Reuters in the state capital of Chandigarh.
"But the blast was so powerful that people in the area at 15 metres' (49 feet) distance were injured," Aujala said.

Aulakh said that the blast destroyed a vehicle belonging to the paramilitary Border Security Forces, killing the driver. He was one of the seven who had died but was earlier believed to have been only wounded.
"Of the 17 people injured, seven had succumbed to their injuries at the last count," Aulakh said.

Asked if he suspected Sikh militants, who have frequently attacked trains in Punjab, Aujala said: "It is too early to suspect anyone. We are trying to lift samples to find out the chemicals used in the bomb."
Some police officials, speaking privately, said the bombing could have been carried out by Moslem separatists based in the adjoining Himalayan state of Jammu and Kashmir.
Kashmiri militants have in the past been suspected of carrying out bombings in Punjab.
Aulakh said the explosion occurred at 1:05 p.m. (0735 GMT) outside the busy railway station.
Sikh militants fighting for an independent homeland in the agriculture-rich region have also targeted trains here, usually inflicting serious casualties.
Police officials said it was the first major incident of violence since the pro-Sikh Akali Dal party took power in the state after local elections in February.
Akali Dal Chief Minister Prakash Singh Badal condemned Friday's attack, saying: "Violence has no place in our democratic setup."

More than 20,000 people have died in Punjab since discontent with New Delhi turned into an armed insurrection after the government sent in troops to flush out militants holed up inside the Golden Temple in Amritsar, the Sikhs' holiest shrine, in June 1984.
